The decision file is already written with ROLLBACK, which the evidence supports: canary 1.1 produced 10 5xx (all on /checkout, 2.07% of 483 checkout requests) while the 3 stable pods produced 0 5xx across 7359 requests; latency is indistinguishable (p50 28 vs 32 ms, p95 96 vs 94 ms, per-route p95/p99 identical), so latency is not the issue. The errors are not a startup artifact — they appear in every 30 s window (1, 3, 3, 3) rather than only 0-30s. Judgement: promoting would scale a ~2% checkout failure rate to 100% of traffic, so rollback is the safer call. Nothing further to verify; finish.

args.summary: Wrote review/B-dashboard-5/decision.json with decision=ROLLBACK. Evidence: canary (v1.1, 1 pod) returned 10 5xx out of 2455 requests (0.41% overall), all concentrated on /checkout (10/483 = 2.07%), while stable (v1.0, 3 pods) returned 0 5xx out of 7359 requests including 1455 checkouts. Latency is a non-issue: canary p50 28ms vs stable 32ms, p95 96 vs 94, and per-route p95/p99 are identical (/browse 27/28, /search 58/60, /checkout 104/106). The errors persist in all four 30s windows (1, 3, 3, 3) rather than only during warm-up, so they are steady-state, not a startup artifact. Judgement: a new, sustained ~2% failure rate on the revenue-critical checkout path that stable does not show is a customer-facing regression, and promoting would expose 4x the traffic to it; blocking the release is the cheaper error.
